name: Cross-sectional equity momentum (winners minus losers)

origin.source_title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency

how_it_works.simple: Buy the stocks that went up the most over the past year and sell the ones that went down the most.
how_it_works.analogy: Like betting on the students with the best grades this year to keep doing well next term.
how_it_works.precise: Rank stocks on past 3 to 12 month returns and hold a long-short portfolio of winners minus losers for 3 to 12 months. Jegadeesh and Titman find significant positive returns not explained by systematic risk, with partial reversal in the following two years. The Fama-French UMD factor uses returns from month t-12 to t-2.

rule: Each month, rank stocks by cumulative return from t-12 to t-2; go long the top 30% and short the bottom 30% (value-weighted within size groups, as in the French UMD factor); hold one month and rebalance.
data_needed: Monthly total returns for a broad stock universe
Or the free UMD factor series from the Kenneth French library
economic_rationale: Investors underreact to firm news and then overreact later, so past winners keep outperforming for some months (Jegadeesh and Titman 1993, 2001).
why_it_might_fail: Momentum crashes after market rebounds from panics (Daniel and Moskowitz 2016); in the French data UMD lost money from 2009 to 2026 (about -0.8% a year) and had a -78% drawdown over its history.

post_publication_evidence: Jegadeesh and Titman (2001, https://doi.org/10.1111/0022-1082.00342) report that momentum profits continued in the 1990s. Over a longer span the French UMD factor's Sharpe ratio fell from about 0.80 (1965 to 1989) to about 0.29 (1993 to 2026), catalog computation. McLean and Pontiff (2016) find that across 97 published stock return predictors, portfolio returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication (https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.12365).

implementations.notes: General event-driven backtester with a pipeline API for ranking stocks; the momentum rule must be written by the user.

relevance.reason: An equity factor rather than an FX strategy; mainly useful as a comparison and as evidence on how momentum decays after publication.
